conviction_note: The in-window event is a statutory FY26 Annual Report from a pre-revenue developer whose cash (A$60.2m at 30 June, A$49m at 31 August) is already public, so the only live content is the status of three September-quarter deliverables the company reaffirmed on 8 September and has not delivered with three sessions left (Project Delivery Plan with an enhanced Ore Reserve, mining contract award, first draw on the A$236m facility); the likeliest print is a timing miss (print_vs_bar -15), but a miss moves this stock little while the Plan landing Sep 28 pm / Sep 29 am carries a fatter right tail, and the stock's sell-the-news record on milestones (FID 0.0%, EPC -1.2%, financing +2.4%) vetoes anything larger, so the net is +0.4.
bar: The company's own stated September-quarter (Q3 2026) deliverables, not EPS: release a Project Delivery Plan with contracted costs, updated economics and an enhanced Ore Reserve and mine life; award the mining contract and mobilise; start rebuilding the plant; first drawdown under the A$236m SFA 'expected to occur in Q3 2026'. Cash bar is A$60.2m at 30 June 2026 (June 5B, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260730/pdf/0726xmx6fybcx7.pdf) and A$49m with nil debt at 31 August 2026 (8 Sep presentation, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260908/pdf/073v93x3q07h0p.pdf, which puts the Plan, the mining contract award and reserve growth in its 'Q3-2026' column). This is a company statement, not a street number. consensus.quarters is empty.
filer_type_check: The baseline says quarterly_report_only (11 Appendix 5B reports, no 4D/4E), and that is right as far as it goes. But BML also lodges a Half Yearly Report (10 Mar 2026 at 20:10) and an Annual Report late each September after the close (2025 Annual Report on 22 Sep 2025 at 17:55, Annual Report on 26 Sep 2024 at 17:57), and the baseline's classifier did not count either. The 2026-09-28 amc event is the FY26 (30 June) Annual Report, not a 5B. It is audited accounts for a pre-production developer and restates cash the 5B already disclosed. So I hunted what the report must say and whether the undelivered September-quarter promises land inside the window, not an EPS bar.
event_check: No annual report is in the 2026 ASX archive yet: the latest lodgement is 18/09/2026, an AGM date notice setting the AGM for 24 Nov 2026 (https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/announcements.do?by=asxCode&asxCode=BML&timeframe=Y&year=2026). The FY26 Annual Report is statutorily due by 30 Sep 2026, and the prior two landed after the close in late September (22/09/2025 17:55 and 26/09/2024 17:57, https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/announcements.do?by=asxCode&asxCode=BML&timeframe=Y&year=2025 and ...&year=2024). So the event is real and nearly certain to fall within 28-30 Sep. The exact day is a vendor date with no company notice behind it. If it lands 29 Sep after the close or on 30 Sep, it is outside this window.
session_check: amc: both prior annual reports were lodged at about 17:55 Sydney, after the 16:00 close (ASX archive 2025 and 2024 URLs above). The baseline's amc is consistent with that. The day itself is not settled.
positioning_check: ASIC aggregate short 0.667% as of 2026-09-21 (lag 4 sessions), down from 0.721% on 2026-09-14 (-0.054pp, mild covering). That is small and not crowded, so there is no squeeze fuel and no sign of a positioned bear. The run-up is -22.3% over 20d and -10.1% over 5d. Most of it lines up with silver falling on 2 Sep (-10.9% that day) and 24 Sep (-6.8%) (Yahoo silver pieces for those dates), so macro drove the fall rather than anything company-specific. The lean of +1.6 is mostly the run-up reversal prior.

findings.finding: Three deliverables Boab set for the September quarter are still missing with three sessions left: the Project Delivery Plan (updated economics on contracted costs plus an enhanced Ore Reserve and mine life at a silver price about 2.3x the FEED's US$27.4/oz), the mining contract award, and the first SFA drawdown. The Plan has already slipped once, from Q2 2026 (15 Jan outlook) to Q3 (1 July update). Either it lands in the window (Sep 28 after the close or Sep 29 before the open), or the Annual Report's subsequent-events note has to show where all three stand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On milestone and timeline news this stock mostly sells the news or shrugs: the 15 Jan 2026 outlook that first set the Plan for Q2 fell -6.25%; the 1 Jul 2026 update that widened the Plan to a reserve and mine-life upgrade rose +4.41% (+16.2% over two sessions, with silver); FID on 17 Dec 2025 was 0.0%; EPC award on 26 May 2026 -1.19%; financing completion on 27 Apr 2026 +2.41% then -3.6% two-day; drilling extensions on 14 Sep 2026 +1.16%. The two prior annual reports sat inside silver-driven runs (26 Sep 2024 AR, then -4.17%; 22 Sep 2025 AR, then +17.33% on a move ASX queried and the company attributed to silver and broker research). The last five 5B quarterlies moved -8.33, -10.53, +7.44, -4.94, 0.0.
findings.why_not_priced: The promise is public; how close the deadline is may not be. If the market expected the Plan inside the window, the stock would not have fallen 10% in five sessions on flat company news with shorts covering rather than building. If it had priced a third slip, you would expect building shorts or a price query, and neither is there. Nobody covers the timing. No broker consensus exists (consensus.quarters empty), and the only wire copy (Kalkine, discoveryalert) repeats 'fully funded, first production H2 2027' with no date on the Plan. The sign is weak because the two branches (Plan lands vs. AR discloses a slip) roughly cancel. Most of what this adds is width, not drift.
findings.independence: Separate primary documents show the same Q3 commitment and the earlier slip: the 15 Jan 2026 Strategic Outlook ('Project Delivery Plan is expected to be completed in Q2 2026', https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260115/pdf/06v8tjg65s0v3h.pdf); the 1 Jul 2026 update ('will release a Project Delivery Plan during the current quarter', https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260701/pdf/0716t81bbw8xg5.pdf); the June-quarter 5B (Plan, mining contract award and 'first drawdown under the SFA is expected to occur in Q3 2026', https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260730/pdf/0726xmx6fybcx7.pdf). All three are company statements, so the independence is in the dates, not the voice. The 14 Sep 2026 drilling release puts further assays in Q4 2026 (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260914/pdf/0741n40vnkfhgy.pdf). That raises the odds the reserve update waits for them, and it is why the central estimate sits near zero.

outside_window.finding: If the Project Delivery Plan lands on 30 Sep, the last day of the quarter, or slips to Q4, the re-rating from an updated reserve and economics at about US$64/oz silver against the FEED's US$27.4/oz (FEED NPV8 A$411m against a market cap of about A$231m at A$0.40) happens after this window. The October 5B, due late October, will also give the first-drawdown status and the September-quarter cash burn against A$49m at 31 August.

baseline_tension: The finding leans the same way as the +1.6 lean only by a hair and is mostly width. The -10% five-day and -22% twenty-day run-up match silver, not company news, and the most likely outcome in the window is a timing miss this stock has shrugged off before. So nothing here beats the run-up control, and the number stays below the lean.
